change: A model or agent that changes (retrained, re-prompted, or given a new tool) is what triggers the gate.
pipeline: The change enters a CI/CD pipeline that already runs tests for functional correctness.
suite: An eval suite is versioned alongside the model so the same tests travel with each change.
capability: The pipeline runs at least one capability eval in CI (illustratively with tools such as Inspect or promptfoo).
adversarial: It also runs at least one adversarial eval, for example an injection-resistance floor (illustratively with Garak or Giskard).
threshold: A threshold that traces to a named failure mode or obligation decides pass or fail.
ship: Above the documented threshold the release passes the gate and ships.
evidence: The eval run emits a structured result: suite id, model version, score, threshold, pass/fail, timestamp.
registry: The structured result is filed against the registry entry, so evidence accrues automatically.
blocked: Below the threshold the eval fails the pipeline and the release does not ship until fixed.
